sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Granulomas are organized collections of activated macrophages that may form in chronic inflammatory conditions.
Caseating granulomas are associated with tuberculosis and some fungal infections; noncaseating granulomas occur in sarcoidosis and other conditions.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Histologic appearance alone is insufficient to confirm organism or cause.
Interpret biopsy alongside microbiology, exposure and the distribution of disease.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Not every noncaseating granuloma indicates sarcoidosis, and not every tuberculous granuloma shows classic caseation.
